<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f0ef826534a90cdf">Why does OPST generate both problems and privileged clues?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopst">On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reduce reliance on human problem banks and give teacher extra solving context while students generate from prompts only. Validate generated tasks through independent re-answering, meaning-preserving rewrites and difficulty filtering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Resolve a generated problem independently to reject inconsistent prompts or answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32770v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.32770-opst/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f0ef826534a90cdf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opst" data-paper-title="On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-36db4c81ae6babb0">Why reject as easy only unanimous matches to the verified candidate answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopst">On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Agreement alone doesn&#x27;t show mastery. All students can agree on the wrong answer. Privileged clues only guide teacher scoring on student prefixes; self-generated problems need independent re-answering and meaning-preserving checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A unanimous wrong number remains useful until compared with the verified candidate answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32770v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.32770-opst/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-36db4c81ae6babb0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opst" data-paper-title="On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-789c0a70700a8a7a">How does OPST easy filtering differ from removing student consensus?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopst">On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only unanimous matches to the candidate answer are too easy. Unanimous disagreement may signal a gap or bad problem. Removing all consensus changes the gate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Identical wrong results don&#x27;t establish mastery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32770v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.32770-opst/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-789c0a70700a8a7a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opst" data-paper-title="On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d8e4b8770738e55">Is OPST EMA β old-teacher momentum or new-student weight?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopst">On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It is new-student weight: after each student update, use (1−β) old teacher + β new student. Normalize per response then average equally. Document formula ambiguity instead of claiming unquestioned exactness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Small β means slowly absorb the student, not almost replace the teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32770v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.32770-opst/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d8e4b8770738e55">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:userarena-optd" data-paper-title="UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-userarena-optd-fa417c42" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd5d72e728c540ac">Why does UserArena report more than next-action accuracy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Auserarena-optd">UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Leiden University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Simulation should preserve trajectory dynamics, cross-session preferences and cohort differences, and reproduce differences between recommendation policies. Local hits aren&#x27;t whole-user fidelity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Good click prediction with wrong long-run interest drift can still distort policy evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30932v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.30932-userarena-optd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd5d72e728c540ac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:userarena-optd" data-paper-title="UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c1b0f08383a3b1a7">Why give only teacher abstract intent and bound it token by token?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Auserarena-optd">UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Leiden University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Whole trajectories leak future products/actions. Filter abstract preferences for teacher only, preserving student deployment input. Compare teacher views on the same prefix, constrain added guidance and ground on actual responses. KL can&#x27;t replace leakage checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Durability preference may be available; next item IDs and purchase outcomes may not.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30932v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.30932-userarena-optd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c1b0f08383a3b1a7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:userarena-optd" data-paper-title="UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3cb76e9a0484bea7">How does OPTD teacher intent differ from giving the student future trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Auserarena-optd">UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Leiden University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only frozen teacher sees abstract intent, excluding concrete action/item identity, price and outcome. Student continues its own prefixes. Trust regions bound effects but don&#x27;t prove no extraction leakage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Lightweight-item preference is allowed, next clicked product is not.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30932v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.30932-userarena-optd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3cb76e9a0484bea7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:userarena-optd" data-paper-title="UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-60fd85e5702a4113">May OPTD grounding replace gold tokens on a student rollout prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Auserarena-optd">UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Leiden University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Grounding uses separate true-prefix logits; teacher views score identical student prefixes. Use feasible lower endpoint per token with KL from mixed to no-intent teacher, not batch-mean reverse KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Injecting the actual next action after a divergent student history is not teacher forcing on a real trajectory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30932v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.30932-userarena-optd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-60fd85e5702a4113">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gift" data-paper-title="GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-gift-0ba87e11" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b123564c01f6717c">Why inspect RL and distillation gradient geometry in GIFT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agift">GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher signal can conflict or add an orthogonal direction. Select by local logit gradients to reduce conflict and narrow supervision rather than imitate every token.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher format preferences can oppose task reward, so inspect the directions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30796v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.30796-gift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b123564c01f6717c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gift" data-paper-title="GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b3048c4edc48d7f1">Why can&#x27;t gradient-based GIFT selection promise permanent absence of conflict?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agift">GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prioritize nonconflicting and orthogonally informative tokens; quotas can require weaker conflicts. Selection isn&#x27;t projection, and normalize by all valid tokens. Local logit geometry doesn&#x27;t guarantee finite shared-parameter updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A subbatch quota larger than conflict-free availability can select the least conflicting extras.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30796v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.30796-gift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b3048c4edc48d7f1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gift" data-paper-title="GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a48523351089a33">How does GIFT token selection differ from projecting teacher gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agift">GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Selected tokens retain original distillation losses; gradients aren&#x27;t rotated. Exact quotas may admit weak conflicts, so there is no universal finite-step safety guarantee.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An accepted position uses its original loss, not a geometrically replaced gradient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30796v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.30796-gift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a48523351089a33">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gift" data-paper-title="GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7126c7fe89d09a9f">Can GIFT renormalize by selected token count?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agift">GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Divide by all valid tokens. Quotas depend on subbatch valid/eligible sets. Follow explicit handling for missing RL and zero teacher gradients rather than automatically treating them as novel directions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Selecting half and dividing by half doubles retained contribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30796v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.30796-gift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7126c7fe89d09a9f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:projected-distillation" data-paper-title="Projected Distillation: On Learning to Solve Hard Problems from Close, Correct Targets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-projected-distillation-64e08dbb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc58ba6017e990bd">Why minimally repair a wrong student response before projected distillation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprojected-distillation">Projected Distillation: On Learning to Solve Hard Problems from Close, Correct Targets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Massachusetts</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Expert prose can be far from student distribution. Minimal edits retain current behavior while correcting what is needed, with independent verification. This is an approximation, not exact most-likely correct output.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correct one wrong symbol instead of replacing the whole derivation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27467v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.27467-projected-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc58ba6017e990bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:projected-distillation" data-paper-title="Projected Distillation: On Learning to Solve Hard Problems from Close, Correct Targets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-89fafaf09dc10a31">Why restrict DPO to edits and SFT to student successes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprojected-distillation">Projected Distillation: On Learning to Solve Hard Problems from Close, Correct Targets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Massachusetts</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Minimal repair preserves generated structure and focuses preference credit on corrections. Repaired and independently correct responses have different provenance. Score both sides under their full causal contexts; shared parameters can still change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If only the last operator is wrong, verify its replacement and contrast the edit rather than imitate all teacher wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27467v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.27467-projected-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-89fafaf09dc10a31">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:projected-distillation" data-paper-title="Projected Distillation: On Learning to Solve Hard Problems from Close, Correct Targets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ee4c6fe883ba19f">How does edited-span DPO differ from SFT on a complete repaired answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprojected-distillation">Projected Distillation: On Learning to Solve Hard Problems from Close, Correct Targets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Massachusetts</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Span DPO contrasts only original and verified edit positions; unchanged text is not directly included. Full SFT is for student-generated successes, not projector repairs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An externally repaired reply is not an autonomous success from this round.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27467v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.27467-projected-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ee4c6fe883ba19f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:projected-distillation" data-paper-title="Projected Distillation: On Learning to Solve Hard Problems from Close, Correct Targets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-09ba8e7510d3cbca">Can edited-span scoring drop the preceding text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprojected-distillation">Projected Distillation: On Learning to Solve Hard Problems from Close, Correct Targets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Massachusetts</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Score each edit under its own complete causal prefix, summing span logp without length averaging. One insertion/deletion side may be empty but pair needs an edit. Zero direct gradient elsewhere does not protect shared weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Editing step three changes step four&#x27;s context; don&#x27;t borrow another response&#x27;s prefix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27467v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.27467-projected-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-09ba8e7510d3cbca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:optd" data-paper-title="On-Policy Transition Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-optd-ae85339e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6e0994774b466ec4">Why doesn&#x27;t inter-layer OPTD only align final predictions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoptd">On-Policy Transition Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final agreement can hide different depth-wise revisions. Supervise shallow-to-deep log-probability increments and retain final OPD. This is prediction paths, not hidden-vector matching.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two models can end on A after very different intermediate changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28048v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.28048-optd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6e0994774b466ec4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:optd" data-paper-title="On-Policy Transition Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-92cd60993660c41f">Why choose candidate tokens once at the final student layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoptd">On-Policy Transition Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Track the same predictions through depth. Independent top-k confounds identity with changes. Use full-vocabulary-normalized log-probability increments plus final OPD, with detach and destination-layer weights, not hidden MSE or exact transition KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If shallow favors A and deep B, retain both identities to trace their rise/fall.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28048v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.28048-optd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-92cd60993660c41f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:optd" data-paper-title="On-Policy Transition Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ffbcd2a8b641010">How does transition supervision differ from independent top-k at each layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoptd">On-Policy Transition Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final student layer chooses fixed token identities for the entire path. Independent sets mix different objects when comparing increments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If shallow top is A and deep top B, subtracting their logp doesn&#x27;t measure A&#x27;s change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28048v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.28048-optd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ffbcd2a8b641010">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:optd" data-paper-title="On-Policy Transition Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a35d4c1e8b97d108">Which OPTD increment endpoints receive gradients and how is practical scale handled?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoptd">On-Policy Transition Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both adjacent student readouts are differentiable. Teacher, candidate weights and correction coefficients are frozen. Appendix sums transitions while main text averages; neither is exact reverse transition KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sum of three transitions cannot silently become a mean at the same objective scale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28048v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.28048-optd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a35d4c1e8b97d108">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ap-opd" data-paper-title="Adaptive Pullback: Reweighting Supervision at Penalty Jumps in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-ap-opd-602f5990" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f27ab2be52c9e3a9">Why does AP-OPD target penalty jumps rather than uniformly high penalties?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aap-opd">Adaptive Pullback: Reweighting Supervision at Penalty Jumps in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Persistent disagreement and sudden local deterioration differ. Compare adjacent original block statistics and attenuate the later block to limit spike dominance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A hard entire response differs from one getting abruptly worse after a particular step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28194v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.28194-ap-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f27ab2be52c9e3a9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ap-opd" data-paper-title="Adaptive Pullback: Reweighting Supervision at Penalty Jumps in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ab6844a2ad8b41b">Why use original block statistics and scale negative coefficients too?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aap-opd">Adaptive Pullback: Reweighting Supervision at Penalty Jumps in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weighted statistics would recursively alter subsequent reference levels. Detect from original positive penalty means but attenuate all signed supervision in the later block. Preserve direction, allow zero weight, and do not interpret threshold as calibrated significance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare block three to block two&#x27;s original level even if block two was already reduced.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28194v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.28194-ap-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ab6844a2ad8b41b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ap-opd" data-paper-title="Adaptive Pullback: Reweighting Supervision at Penalty Jumps in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d1e8642985152690">How does AP-OPD attenuation differ from dropping outlier tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aap-opd">Adaptive Pullback: Reweighting Supervision at Penalty Jumps in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Apply one factor to all signed coefficients in a block, preserving signs and including negatives. Dropping tokens is a different selection rule. The detector is not a calibrated significance test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Negative log ratios in the later block are also scaled.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28194v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.28194-ap-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d1e8642985152690">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ap-opd" data-paper-title="Adaptive Pullback: Reweighting Supervision at Penalty Jumps in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-296cc09fc542365b">Can the next AP-OPD boundary use previously attenuated statistics?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aap-opd">Adaptive Pullback: Reweighting Supervision at Penalty Jumps in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Always detect from original unweighted means/variance to avoid recursive distortion. No renormalization or hidden floor; previous mean zero may produce zero weight. Sample variance needs enough tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Detecting from an already reduced block can create artificial jumps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28194v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.28194-ap-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-296cc09fc542365b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:simopd" data-paper-title="SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-simopd-1a5a0435" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-10f0cd80f01cd072">Why can SimOPD handle different teacher/student hidden dimensions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asimopd">SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each space compares current reply to paired historical replies. Distill distributions indexed by shared answer identities rather than subtract cross-model vectors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 100-dimensional model and wider model can both rank similarities to the same old answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23306v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23306-simopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-10f0cd80f01cd072">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:simopd" data-paper-title="SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-67acf86af9d51b82">Why not project teacher/student hidden states into one coordinate system first?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asimopd">SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compute similarities in each own space, match distributions over paired historical IDs. Freeze teacher/bank and maintain synchronized FIFO. A single historical point cannot provide relational supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two teachers can agree a reply is closer to historical A than B without identical coordinates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23306v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23306-simopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67acf86af9d51b82">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:simopd" data-paper-title="SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-115407df068b5178">How does relational SimOPD differ from hidden-state MSE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asimopd">SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MSE requires comparable coordinates. Relationship matching preserves geometry without forcing coordinates and differs from vocabulary distillation: targets are similarities to historical answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rotating a map changes coordinates without changing city distances.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23306v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23306-simopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-115407df068b5178">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:simopd" data-paper-title="SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7fe30fc164756b21">When does SimOPD enqueue and why reject a one-item bank?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asimopd">SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>After optimization enqueue frozen paired representations captured before it, using synchronized FIFO; first batch only warms up. One bank item makes the distribution constant and uninformative. Only current student representation gets gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Misaligned FIFO positions compare relations to different answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23306v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23306-simopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7fe30fc164756b21">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gr-opd" data-paper-title="GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-gr-opd-372c128f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c32b70c1d0bfe7a4">Why pool token feedback into sequence scores in GR-OPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agr-opd">GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local teacher confidence needn&#x27;t mean good overall reasoning. Discount and aggregate sequence feedback, then compare same-prompt replies for relative credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher preference for formatting tokens doesn&#x27;t make a wrong trajectory preferable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23042v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23042-gr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c32b70c1d0bfe7a4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gr-opd" data-paper-title="GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c13ef09cde51e17">Why retain mean pressure after group centering?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agr-opd">GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pure centering keeps only within-group ranking and can erase shared correction. Add mean pressure before broadcasting credit to actions. Discount, standardization and clipping alter the practical estimator&#x27;s guarantees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>All replies can be similarly unsupported; centering nearly zeroes them while mean term preserves correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23042v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23042-gr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0c13ef09cde51e17">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gr-opd" data-paper-title="GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6de85a3be3e409a7">How does retaining mean pressure differ from pure group centering?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agr-opd">GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pure centering removes teacher&#x27;s common direction across replies. An extra mean term preserves some shared pressure; its coefficient may be zero. Treat configurations separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If every reply diverges from teacher, relative ranks alone hide shared mismatch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23042v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23042-gr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6de85a3be3e409a7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gr-opd" data-paper-title="GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-731099dc5565deac">Does GR-OPD average tokens globally or per response?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agr-opd">GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Average valid actor tokens within each response then average replies equally. Clip and discount-normalize feedback first. Freeze teacher/old policy/credit. Bare theoretical sums don&#x27;t imply guarantees under practical clipping and reuse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Length alone doesn&#x27;t give a response more total weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23042v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23042-gr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-731099dc5565deac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ig-opd" data-paper-title="Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-ig-opd-f18f6a41" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-30c73194464ab10f">Why judge IG-OPD queries after retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aig-opd">Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher phrasing preferences can dislike effective searches. Changes in answer support after retrieval indicate useful information. Answer probes are training-only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An awkward query retrieving key evidence can be valuable despite its wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20664v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.20664-ig-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-30c73194464ab10f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ig-opd" data-paper-title="Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4cddf433bec13e2a">Why budget with absolute gain but update queries with signed gain?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aig-opd">Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Large positive or negative changes deserve supervision; action credit must distinguish help from harm. The additive parts act on different sets. Answers belong to frozen training probes only; long final replies must not absorb short-query budgets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Misleading results can justify large correction but negative rather than positive direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20664v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.20664-ig-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4cddf433bec13e2a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ig-opd" data-paper-title="Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b103877b7ce93590">Do ITC and IQC change credit magnitude or direction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aig-opd">Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ITC budgets turns by absolute gain; IQC uses signed gain to calibrate action tokens. Large negative gain merits attention, not positive reinforcement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Misleading retrieval that lowers confidence needs correction, not reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20664v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.20664-ig-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b103877b7ce93590">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ig-opd" data-paper-title="Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-856d0f74b3c8069f">Why is IQC outside ITC, and what does λ=0 mean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aig-opd">Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Total action credit is warm-up coefficient times gain, not multiplied again by turn budget. λ=0 gives equal turn budget, not equal token weight. Final response gain is zero but base distillation remains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A short call and long answer with equal budgets have different token weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20664v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.20664-ig-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-856d0f74b3c8069f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:divergence-routed-opd" data-paper-title="Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-divergence-routed-opd-a4becc18" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8206592939f8cdfd">Why add forward KL at high-disagreement positions in DrOPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adivergence-routed-opd">Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reverse-KL gradients depend on student mass and can be weak on teacher modes students nearly ignore. Forward KL restores missing coverage locally while retaining RKL everywhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher-supported digits with near-zero student mass need an extra coverage signal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19572v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.19572-divergence-routed-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8206592939f8cdfd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:divergence-routed-opd" data-paper-title="Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3312d2d758d1406c">Why keep RKL everywhere and add FKL only at high disagreement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adivergence-routed-opd">Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>RKL imitates covered modes but can weakly move near-absent teacher modes. JS routing localizes FKL&#x27;s coverage correction. Union support, detached advantages and PPO matter; not switching all KL or only updating the sampled token.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If teacher strongly prefers A and student only B, extra local FKL can lift A.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19572v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.19572-divergence-routed-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3312d2d758d1406c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:divergence-routed-opd" data-paper-title="Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fcb1fb07ad2072fa">How does DrOPD routing differ from replacing the whole loss with forward KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adivergence-routed-opd">Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Add FKL only on routed positions and keep RKL globally. Full replacement changes concentration/coverage elsewhere. PPO candidate-advantage updates also aren&#x27;t a static two-KL gradient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Low-disagreement format tokens keep the original objective; difficult positions get extra correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19572v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.19572-divergence-routed-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fcb1fb07ad2072fa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:divergence-routed-opd" data-paper-title="Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-96d798d1719d8dcf">Should ties at DrOPD&#x27;s kth-largest JS be broken to keep exactly K?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adivergence-routed-opd">Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Retain all at threshold, possibly more than K. Compute K from valid positions as specified; K=0 adds no FKL. Deduplicate and renormalize the top-k teacher/student union. Freeze teacher, route and advantage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Don&#x27;t drop tied boundary positions to force an exact quota.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19572v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.19572-divergence-routed-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96d798d1719d8dcf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:state-opd" data-paper-title="State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-state-opd-163aa0d8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1d24b1b78b89d80d">Why hide old reasoning from the State-OPD teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Astate-opd">State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Old reasoning can be wrong. The teacher sees executed actions/observations to avoid inheriting false narratives; student still sees its full history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher should trust a tool&#x27;s failure result over previous reasoning claiming success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13238">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13238-state-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1d24b1b78b89d80d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:state-opd" data-paper-title="State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d262ea667bfbfb6">Why omit old reasoning for the teacher and not execute extra actions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Astate-opd">State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Executed observations are real even when student reasoning is mistaken. Use them for teacher state while student retains full context. Compare oversampled candidates at the same high-entropy state; executing them breaks alignment. Entropy is vocabulary-wide.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use actual click results instead of mistaken prior narrative, and score extra proposed clicks without pressing every button.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13238">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13238-state-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d262ea667bfbfb6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:state-opd" data-paper-title="State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-79b8351df47c84f9">How does high-entropy oversampling differ from executing all extra actions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Astate-opd">State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generate extra reasoning/actions for training comparison, but execute none of them. The actual environment follows the original trace. Executing them changes state visitation and budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scoring alternative tools doesn&#x27;t mean using every one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13238">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13238-state-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-79b8351df47c84f9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:state-opd" data-paper-title="State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-99462504c15e1d5e">Can sampled-token surprisal replace State-OPD entropy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Astate-opd">State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Average full-vocabulary entropies across tokens and follow the stated state selection/count formula. Keep sampled-K1 double clipping rather than heuristic teacher ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sampled rare word does not imply high entropy of the whole distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13238">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13238-state-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-99462504c15e1d5e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:semi-opd" data-paper-title="When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-semi-opd-2bdbc401" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7b72ead50a6a5959">Why fix trajectories generated by the initial student in Semi-OPD?</h2>
