<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asemi-opd">When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UCLA / NVIDIA（论文注明实习）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One collection and teacher-scoring pass saves future costs. Train on fixed visited states, while acknowledging later policy drift means data are no longer freshly on-policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reuse initially common error prefixes without collecting newer ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11291-semi-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7b72ead50a6a5959">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:semi-opd" data-paper-title="When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a786e75dec63a25d">Why recompute student probabilities and advantages despite cached teacher scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asemi-opd">When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UCLA / NVIDIA（论文注明实习）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed trajectories and teacher outputs can be reused, but student probabilities and gaps change after updates. Stale directions distort the objective. Offline student rollouts save compute, not fresh on-policy sampling every step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A once-underweighted token may exceed teacher support; old positive credit would still push it up.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11291-semi-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a786e75dec63a25d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:semi-opd" data-paper-title="When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bae5a82668cbabbb">Why cache teacher labels but not advantages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asemi-opd">When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UCLA / NVIDIA（论文注明实习）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Frozen teacher scores remain valid for fixed prefixes. Advantage also depends on current student logp and must refresh. A cached advantage is a stale objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>When student support rises, the teacher gap shrinks despite unchanged teacher score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11291-semi-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bae5a82668cbabbb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:semi-opd" data-paper-title="When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3ee4c2ca0a72c5d9">What must remain immutable in the Semi-OPD cache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asemi-opd">When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UCLA / NVIDIA（论文注明实习）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Align prompts, responses, teacher scores and masks. Refresh only current student scores and detached advantages each step. This doesn&#x27;t guarantee long-term coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Deleting a token while reusing old indexed scores misaligns supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11291-semi-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3ee4c2ca0a72c5d9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-learning-signals" data-paper-title="Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-opd-learning-signals-810b86e8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d1917373fe01bd8">Why inspect both loss and gradients in OPD Learning Signals?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-learning-signals">Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Large residual divergence can coexist with weak updates. Combine loss, pre-clip gradients, parameter motion and representation similarity to diagnose stagnation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Distributions can differ while current parameterization yields little usable gradient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11247-opd-learning-signals/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d1917373fe01bd8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-learning-signals" data-paper-title="Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f79a618fa17f4eb1">Why doesn&#x27;t high residual OPD loss guarantee learnability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-learning-signals">Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A numeric gap differs from gradient that can move parameters; saturation/coverage may weaken it. Jointly inspect pre-clip gradients, split estimates, parameter movement and representations. Nonpositive denominators are undefined. Diagnostics aren&#x27;t causes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Loss can remain high while gradients and parameter updates are nearly zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11247-opd-learning-signals/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f79a618fa17f4eb1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-learning-signals" data-paper-title="Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b50c37bc57652503">Do occupancy and CKA diagnostics prove why training stalled?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-learning-signals">Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. They describe patterns among sampling, updates and representations. Causal attribution needs controls or assumptions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar layers and slow learning occurring together don&#x27;t establish one caused the other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11247-opd-learning-signals/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b50c37bc57652503">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-learning-signals" data-paper-title="Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b64d4e29f8e4c3c3">What if a learning-signal proxy has nonpositive loss or split denominator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-learning-signals">Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mark the ratio undefined, not zero-filled. Compute CKA from per-prompt averages centered across prompts at specified precision. Use gradients before clipping.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A negative split gradient dot product should not become a positive occupancy by absolute value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11247-opd-learning-signals/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b64d4e29f8e4c3c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sipo" data-paper-title="SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-sipo-d20b9ca6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9d03a13157ecc4b4">Why provide positive and negative privileged contexts for each SIPO rollout?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asipo">SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher logp differences aim to cancel common confidence/style and expose informative token evidence. Environment reward still guides the task. Student sampling sees neither privilege.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If both teachers favor a filler phrase, subtraction reduces that common bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36742">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.36742-sipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9d03a13157ecc4b4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sipo" data-paper-title="SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-272d9b14d8ce1c73">Why use two SIPO teacher views rather than one correct hint?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asipo">SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Contrast log probabilities on identical student rollouts to reduce shared confidence and style. Environmental reward supplies main direction and dense evidence redistributes token credit. Both views are training-only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Both teachers may prefer politeness but diverge on key evidence; contrast downweights the shared style.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36742">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.36742-sipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-272d9b14d8ce1c73">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sipo" data-paper-title="SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a7a2fc7c83630be">What assumption differs between SIPO contrast and one privileged teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asipo">SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Single-teacher confidence can include irrelevant effects. Contrast aims to isolate conditioning differences, but poorly designed contexts still mislead and are not independent truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Swapping irrelevant wording needn&#x27;t produce a useful solving contrast.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36742">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.36742-sipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a7a2fc7c83630be">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sipo" data-paper-title="SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-24081935570818df">Can SIPO have token signal when all group rewards are equal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asipo">SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Yes. Centered contrast evidence can be nonzero with zero outcome advantage. Gold stays in teacher/evaluator only, not rollout.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A failed group can receive directional teacher evidence without becoming autonomous successes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36742">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.36742-sipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24081935570818df">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ride-opd" data-paper-title="The Teacher Is a Direction, Not a Destination: Extrapolating RL-Induced Representation Residuals in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-ride-opd-b6296fc3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7230b8ff5992213f">Does RIDE extrapolate output probabilities or hidden residuals?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aride-opd">The Teacher Is a Direction, Not a Destination: Extrapolating RL-Induced Representation Residuals in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It compares RL teacher with pre-RL base per layer/token, then regresses the student to base plus amplified residual. This is representational change, not logit ratios.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Extend a learned layer direction rather than multiply favored word probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36484">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.36484-ride/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7230b8ff5992213f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ride-opd" data-paper-title="The Teacher Is a Direction, Not a Destination: Extrapolating RL-Induced Representation Residuals in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9eaccf1ab5755fc3">Why isn&#x27;t hidden-residual extrapolation equivalent to increasing output probability ratios?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aride-opd">The Teacher Is a Direction, Not a Destination: Extrapolating RL-Induced Representation Residuals in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The target is per-layer/token base plus scaled RL-teacher shift, an internal path probabilities do not preserve. Freeze teacher/base. α above one does not ensure capability beyond teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Extend RL&#x27;s layer displacement rather than amplify all teacher-preferred output words.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36484">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.36484-ride/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9eaccf1ab5755fc3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ride-opd" data-paper-title="The Teacher Is a Direction, Not a Destination: Extrapolating RL-Induced Representation Residuals in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0302ec7605024b73">Does representation extrapolation with α&gt;1 guarantee outperforming the teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aride-opd">The Teacher Is a Direction, Not a Destination: Extrapolating RL-Induced Representation Residuals in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Extending the direction may magnify benefits or move outside reliable states. Evaluate independently; farther geometry is not higher ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Overshooting can destroy information despite extending the same direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36484">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.36484-ride/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0302ec7605024b73">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ride-opd" data-paper-title="The Teacher Is a Direction, Not a Destination: Extrapolating RL-Induced Representation Residuals in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c27131a205381263">Why stop gradients through RIDE teacher and base?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aride-opd">The Teacher Is a Direction, Not a Destination: Extrapolating RL-Induced Representation Residuals in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The target is a fixed RL change; updating its branches makes residual drift. Align layers, tokens and dimensions before subtracting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Student error must not move the teacher target rather than update the student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36484">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.36484-ride/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c27131a205381263">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oasis-opsd" data-paper-title="Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-oasis-opsd-27f4197e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec1a94a3565cdcc0">Why separate OASIS scaffold and teacher context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoasis-opsd">Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · North South University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use the shortest verified trajectory for supervision locations, preferably another unverified attempt for teacher context. Where to learn and what extra context to use are independent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A concise success can anchor positions while a longer attempt provides alternative clues.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37915">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37915-oasis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ec1a94a3565cdcc0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oasis-opsd" data-paper-title="Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e59a6d301d00681">Why can an unverified attempt be teacher context but not scaffold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoasis-opsd">Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · North South University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A scaffold fixes a credible student trajectory; teacher context only provides comparison clues. Unverified attempts aren&#x27;t correct labels. No verified rollout means no training signal, and final verification doesn&#x27;t reveal gold to students.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Score prefixes of a concise verified response while allowing the teacher to reference a longer exploration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37915">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37915-oasis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e59a6d301d00681">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oasis-opsd" data-paper-title="Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3f6085d4cc26e952">Why require a verifier if OASIS has no gold solution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoasis-opsd">Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · North South University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It needs a verified successful rollout before selecting a scaffold. Absence of gold steps does not remove correctness checks. With none verified, emit no signal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The shortest unchecked answer is not automatically a valid scaffold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37915">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37915-oasis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3f6085d4cc26e952">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oasis-opsd" data-paper-title="Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea4b4ea58811e49f">Should OASIS order by length before or after checking eligibility?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoasis-opsd">Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · North South University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Verify first, then choose the shortest eligible trajectory. Track scaffold and teacher context separately and hide future answers from student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A one-line wrong result must not beat a longer verified solution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37915">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37915-oasis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea4b4ea58811e49f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ipd" data-paper-title="Interpolated Policy Distillation: A Controllable Continuum Between Off-Policy and On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-ipd-4481efec" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cac94113033ac8b7">Why interpolate IPD teacher/student sampling distributions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aipd">Interpolated Policy Distillation: A Controllable Continuum Between Off-Policy and On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat Vision, Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pure student and teacher states trade coverage differently. Mix conditional policies continuously at each state; γ controls sample source distribution, not merely loss weighting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Let some steps follow student tendencies and other steps gain teacher-supported options.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37170">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37170-ipd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cac94113033ac8b7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ipd" data-paper-title="Interpolated Policy Distillation: A Controllable Continuum Between Off-Policy and On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b2efc7ad19f40b08">Why isn&#x27;t mixing each token probability the same as selecting one model for the whole reply?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aipd">Interpolated Policy Distillation: A Controllable Continuum Between Off-Policy and On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat Vision, Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Interpolate at every updated prefix; sampled tokens change later states. Choosing a model once gives a different sequence law, and averaging logits is also different. Endpoint checks do not validate the paper&#x27;s speculative sampler.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sample a teacher-favored token first, then remix under the new prefix rather than fix a source for the rest.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37170">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37170-ipd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b2efc7ad19f40b08">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ipd" data-paper-title="Interpolated Policy Distillation: A Controllable Continuum Between Off-Policy and On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc070c60c12b0237">Is token-level mixing equivalent to choosing one model per rollout?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aipd">Interpolated Policy Distillation: A Controllable Continuum Between Off-Policy and On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat Vision, Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Tokenwise mixtures can combine both preferences within a sequence; one source per rollout produces a different joint state distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Student-like first step and teacher-like second may be reached differently under fixed rollout source.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37170">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37170-ipd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc070c60c12b0237">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ipd" data-paper-title="Interpolated Policy Distillation: A Controllable Continuum Between Off-Policy and On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d048feb0beeb9dd5">Do local IPD endpoint checks include speculative high-throughput sampling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aipd">Interpolated Policy Distillation: A Controllable Continuum Between Off-Policy and On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat Vision, Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Exact token mixture checks endpoints, normalization and total variation. γ=0 student, γ=1 teacher. Verification-aware speculative sampler and full training remain unreproduced.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Calculating a mixture vector doesn&#x27;t establish paper sampling throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37170">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37170-ipd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d048feb0beeb9dd5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:flowmap-opd" data-paper-title="FlowMap-OPD: Rollout-Kernel Separation for On-Policy Distillation of Few-Step Flow-Map Generators" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-flowmap-opd-fd47b0da" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-56ef347f59071d0c">Why separate rollout distribution and optimization kernel in FlowMap-OPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aflowmap-opd">FlowMap-OPD: Rollout-Kernel Separation for On-Policy Distillation of Few-Step Flow-Map Generators</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Georgia Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sampling supplies states with specified marginals; a local kernel compares teacher/student flows or velocities. Separate data provision from gradients rather than backpropagating through sampling arbitrarily.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Freeze a sampled intermediate state, then compare local predictions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37851">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37851-flowmap-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-56ef347f59071d0c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:flowmap-opd" data-paper-title="FlowMap-OPD: Rollout-Kernel Separation for On-Policy Distillation of Few-Step Flow-Map Generators" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4852debd06b0bfd3">Why freeze rollout states for kernel gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aflowmap-opd">FlowMap-OPD: Rollout-Kernel Separation for On-Policy Distillation of Few-Step Flow-Map Generators</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Georgia Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rollout supplies required marginals; kernel compares flows or velocity at those states. Differentiating through generation adds unspecified trajectory terms. Detached states can be recollected from later policies, not permanently fixed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sample intermediate states, freeze them for one local teacher comparison, and don&#x27;t backpropagate through entire sampling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37851">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37851-flowmap-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4852debd06b0bfd3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:flowmap-opd" data-paper-title="FlowMap-OPD: Rollout-Kernel Separation for On-Policy Distillation of Few-Step Flow-Map Generators" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-645bf5c6a9169235">How does detaching states differ from end-to-end differentiation through the sampler?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aflowmap-opd">FlowMap-OPD: Rollout-Kernel Separation for On-Policy Distillation of Few-Step Flow-Map Generators</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Georgia Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Detach trains student kernel parameters only. Differentiating through states adds dependency gradients and changes the estimator despite equal scalar loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Current model may affect both states and predictions; freezing states deliberately cuts the former path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37851">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37851-flowmap-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-645bf5c6a9169235">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:flowmap-opd" data-paper-title="FlowMap-OPD: Rollout-Kernel Separation for On-Policy Distillation of Few-Step Flow-Map Generators" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">

<h2 id="qa-4d68bfc6fd93ff35">Does local FlowMap train a real image generator?</h2>

<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Georgia Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:drift-opd" data-paper-title="DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-drift-opd-b3b01276" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-70c7f54da4753f4c">Why add future potential beyond current chunk distillation in DriftOPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adrift-opd">DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actions alter future robot states. One-step matching misses downstream effects. Sequential reverse KL includes a future term estimated from offline demonstration critic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A plausible grasp can prevent later placement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00317">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00317-drift-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-70c7f54da4753f4c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:drift-opd" data-paper-title="DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1bd738afe55776dc">Why add future potential to current chunk reverse KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adrift-opd">DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Immediate matching cannot capture state transitions. A demonstration-trained critic approximates long-horizon effects to retain timing in sequential decomposition. Coverage/critic accuracy matter; no local environment validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two grabs look teacher-like now, but one puts the object out of reach later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00317">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00317-drift-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1bd738afe55776dc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:drift-opd" data-paper-title="DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-43dfa00e793b7ee1">How does future potential differ from an immediate reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adrift-opd">DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It estimates downstream outcomes within a sequence decomposition; immediate reward rates current behavior. Critic approximation matters and adding value is not exact sequence KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Lifting the object earns immediate credit even if placement becomes impossible.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00317">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00317-drift-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-43dfa00e793b7ee1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:drift-opd" data-paper-title="DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-470a921fb5aecf61">Does local DriftOPD execute a robotics closed loop?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adrift-opd">DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It verifies objective decomposition and teacher detach. Real work needs an offline-trained future critic, chunk/state alignment and environment evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A computed potential term does not show a robot completed the task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dr-opd" data-paper-title="Dr. OPD: Learning What to Follow for Optimal On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-dr-opd-97941784" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e8d09aba2b99ef7e">Why does Dr. OPD give teacher tokens different weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adr-opd">Dr. OPD: Learning What to Follow for Optimal On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rutgers University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixing key reasoning matters more than rephrasing. A bilevel approximation weights by expected post-update student reward, not just disagreement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>At equal probability gap, correcting an operator may matter more than changing a connective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38025">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.38025-dr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e8d09aba2b99ef7e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dr-opd" data-paper-title="Dr. OPD: Learning What to Follow for Optimal On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7abf58626c0e76d6">Why weight by downstream reward JVP rather than disagreement size alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adr-opd">Dr. OPD: Learning What to Follow for Optimal On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rutgers University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Large gaps may be stylistic. JVP estimates reward sensitivity along correction, then closed-form weights are bounded and normalized for OPD. Local reward and approximation do not prove global causal contribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher and student can disagree on an operator and politeness, but only one affects task reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38025">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.38025-dr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7abf58626c0e76d6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dr-opd" data-paper-title="Dr. OPD: Learning What to Follow for Optimal On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-98aef755078f6688">How does reward JVP weighting differ from ranking by KL disagreement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adr-opd">Dr. OPD: Learning What to Follow for Optimal On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rutgers University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Disagreement measures distance; JVP estimates downstream reward change along a direction. Combine gap and value, but a local gradient isn&#x27;t independent correctness evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A large stylistic disagreement can have weak reward effect.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38025">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.38025-dr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-98aef755078f6688">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dr-opd" data-paper-title="Dr. OPD: Learning What to Follow for Optimal On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-370359f1be3a4044">What order should Dr. OPD use for weights and student updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adr-opd">Dr. OPD: Learning What to Follow for Optimal On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rutgers University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Solve weights from fixed batch signals, clip and mean-normalize, then update student by weighted RKL. Do not differentiate the student through weight selection. Local d×g is a proxy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choose supervision positions before the student step rather than changing the selector with that step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38025">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.38025-dr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-370359f1be3a4044">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lspd" data-paper-title="An RL View of OPD: Least Square Policy Distillation for Sample-Efficient LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-lspd-3161a2b9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d188b7e250db6eeb">Why treat teacher–student logp gaps as robust residuals in LSPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alspd">An RL View of OPD: Least Square Policy Distillation for Sample-Efficient LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Squared loss shrinks ordinary gaps; Huber-like linear tails limit gradients from extreme ones. Residual regression can reuse older trajectories.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rare token&#x27;s huge log gap should not dominate a batch indefinitely.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35505">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.35505-lspd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d188b7e250db6eeb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lspd" data-paper-title="An RL View of OPD: Least Square Policy Distillation for Sample-Efficient LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-940f981ab925625c">Why use a quadratic center with Huber tails instead of squared loss throughout?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alspd">An RL View of OPD: Least Square Policy Distillation for Sample-Efficient LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Quadratic shrinks small logp gaps while linear tails bound outlier influence and retain correction direction. Average responses equally. Reused old traces are not fresh current-policy samples.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One teacher-improbable token can dominate squared loss; robust tails curb it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35505">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.35505-lspd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-940f981ab925625c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lspd" data-paper-title="An RL View of OPD: Least Square Policy Distillation for Sample-Efficient LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6facb14ce3c65e7b">How does robust LSPD behave in tails compared with reverse KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alspd">An RL View of OPD: Least Square Policy Distillation for Sample-Efficient LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It explicitly limits residual slope; KL is defined through distribution/probability weights. Clipping KL isn&#x27;t equivalent. Replay also changes state provenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Doubling tail residual changes linear and unbounded quadratic gradients differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35505">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.35505-lspd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6facb14ce3c65e7b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lspd" data-paper-title="An RL View of OPD: Least Square Policy Distillation for Sample-Efficient LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ef6042f7787ae37">How handle teacher gradients and lengths in LSPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alspd">An RL View of OPD: Least Square Policy Distillation for Sample-Efficient LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freeze teacher logp. Average differentiable student gaps over valid tokens per response, then responses equally, with specified entropy subtraction. Registry presence doesn&#x27;t prove executable Evolve.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Long replies do not automatically receive twice the weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35505">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.35505-lspd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ef6042f7787ae37">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:recursive-opsd" data-paper-title="Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-recursive-opsd-defa1333" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0187dfcc3ef0ff80">How does Recursive OPSD DCE keep teacher aligned to student updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arecursive-opsd">Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI / University of California, Riverside</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both use current shared weights, teacher additionally sees the reference solution and is detached. Updated weights become both views next round, not a separately trained or initial teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A newly learned correction is available to the next privileged teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:recursive-opsd" data-paper-title="Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1cc48c02b9ecad3b">Why impose different gold boundaries on DCE and SRCL although both update one model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arecursive-opsd">Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI / University of California, Riverside</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>DCE uses current privileged teacher to score actual prefixes, then refreshes both roles after updates. SRCL rewrites its own answer without gold and validates afterward. Giving gold to rewriter changes self-revision into copying. No second teacher is independently trained.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Score a student attempt using a reference solution, then let it shorten its own response with correctness checked only afterward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30652">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.30652-recursive-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1cc48c02b9ecad3b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:recursive-opsd" data-paper-title="Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-641d1a70b1ad6f69">How does SRCL rewriting differ from showing a teacher gold to rewrite?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arecursive-opsd">Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI / University of California, Riverside</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rewrite sees only problem and its own response. Gold is for acceptance. Require shorter, self-contained, naturally ended and correct outputs to avoid mistaking privileged copying for autonomous revision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not include the reference solution in the shortening prompt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30652">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.30652-recursive-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-641d1a70b1ad6f69">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:recursive-opsd" data-paper-title="Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4be18f8110303e1d">What if no shorter revision qualifies in Recursive OPSD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arecursive-opsd">Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI / University of California, Riverside</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Run DCE only; don&#x27;t force failed or longer rewrites into SFT. Identify prompt-role differences in frozen teacher controls; the local assistant-side arm isn&#x27;t the original user-side OPSD baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A correct but longer answer does not pass SRCL and must stay excluded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30652">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.30652-recursive-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4be18f8110303e1d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gamma-opd" data-paper-title="Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-gamma-opd-41117d94" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f5cddebb5119335">Why add temporal credit to Gamma-OPD instead of only immediate log gaps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agamma-opd">Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University / DiDi Voyager Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Choices shape future sequence. Discounted future teacher gaps inform current credit, with verifiable return constraining direction. This isn&#x27;t only immediate imitation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An early branch can cause several later divergences that its local log gap underestimates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16937">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16937-gamma-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f5cddebb5119335">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
