<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gamma-opd" data-paper-title="Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fca6a68c2c9769d1">Why propagate teacher credit backward and add verifiable advantage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agamma-opd">Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University / DiDi Voyager Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later teacher evidence captures effects of early actions; verified outcomes align imitation with task returns. Teacher preference isn&#x27;t correctness. Local formula checks don&#x27;t establish capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An early bad choice may cause several later gaps; credit it upstream while still requiring final verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16937">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16937-gamma-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fca6a68c2c9769d1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gamma-opd" data-paper-title="Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7cf19f73d80e4b13">How does discounted teacher credit differ from adding unbounded outcome reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agamma-opd">Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University / DiDi Voyager Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Discounting carries sequential distillation; bounded advantage controls strength of verified outcomes. Arbitrary reward weights change the balance without proving one better.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A giant terminal reward should not overwhelm temporal guidance without limits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16937">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16937-gamma-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7cf19f73d80e4b13">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gamma-opd" data-paper-title="Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a237d622e61307eb">What does the local Gamma-OPD kernel verify?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agamma-opd">Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University / DiDi Voyager Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Discounted propagation and bounded reward, not full language model training. Preserve order, terminal masks and frozen teacher signals. Shuffling tokens cannot verify temporal credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Moving future credit to another response loses trajectory meaning even when sums are computable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16937">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16937-gamma-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a237d622e61307eb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:route-opd" data-paper-title="Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-route-opd-eaed8417" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-219b65a5fa68be33">Why distinguish source and destination tokens in RouteOPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroute-opd">Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Student-overestimated items have excess mass, underestimated items need mass. Explicit transport identifies where corrections come from and go instead of indiscriminate matching.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Move mass from overpreferred wording to a teacher-supported key digit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08337">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.08337-route-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-219b65a5fa68be33">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:route-opd" data-paper-title="Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2e92fef1b286ea86">Why isn&#x27;t transport equivalent to boosting every high-probability teacher token?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroute-opd">Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Select sources/destinations by student over/underestimation relative to teacher, not absolute teacher mass. This traces corrections and conserves probability. Interpretability doesn&#x27;t prove teacher correctness; control support and evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An already popular word in both models may need no boost; a teacher-supported overlooked word can receive mass.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08337">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.08337-route-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2e92fef1b286ea86">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:route-opd" data-paper-title="Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-349dbfa38577b4a5">How does transporting mass differ from replacing the student distribution with teacher probabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroute-opd">Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Transport addresses selected discrepancies, not every coordinate. Require nonnegativity, conservation and defined source/destination; ordinary softmax isn&#x27;t routing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Unrouted candidates can remain unchanged, unlike full replacement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08337">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.08337-route-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-349dbfa38577b4a5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:route-opd" data-paper-title="Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a0675a60c2b363d9">What invariants should RouteOPD transport check?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroute-opd">Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Never remove more mass than available; additions equal removals; final probabilities nonnegative and normalized. No transport at zero gap. A kernel doesn&#x27;t reproduce teacher-model training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing one unit and adding only half breaks normalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08337">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.08337-route-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a0675a60c2b363d9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opdvr" data-paper-title="OPDVR: On-Policy Distillation with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-opdvr-c33841ab" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-798acb388704187c">Why use a verifier to correct OPDVR teacher reward signs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopdvr">OPDVR: On-Policy Distillation with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LeapLab, Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher/student log ratios can oppose trajectory correctness. Retain only sign-consistent credit to avoid reinforcing errors or suppressing correct trajectories.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not punish a different correct solution just because the teacher dislikes it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24696">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.24696-opdvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-798acb388704187c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opdvr" data-paper-title="OPDVR: On-Policy Distillation with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fbc2e745458cd71">Why retain only nonnegative teacher signal for success and nonpositive for failure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopdvr">OPDVR: On-Policy Distillation with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LeapLab, Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token ratios can conflict with terminal outcome. One-sided ReLU uses verifiable correctness to gate implicit reward, not add a standalone RL loss. Coarse labels don&#x27;t prove each token and remain scoring-only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Suppress a negative imitation signal for a correct alternative without requiring teacher wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24696">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.24696-opdvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1fbc2e745458cd71">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opdvr" data-paper-title="OPDVR: On-Policy Distillation with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5f74d21096cee1c9">How does OPDVR differ from adding another RL loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopdvr">OPDVR: On-Policy Distillation with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LeapLab, Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It removes the inconsistent part of implicit reward rather than mixing two losses with compensating weights. The objectives differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Zero out positive teacher reward on an error rather than add a negative term hoping it cancels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24696">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.24696-opdvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5f74d21096cee1c9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opdvr" data-paper-title="OPDVR: On-Policy Distillation with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c1bc8524df74367">Which half-axis does OPDVR retain for correct and wrong trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopdvr">OPDVR: On-Policy Distillation with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LeapLab, Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Correct keeps nonnegative log ratios; wrong keeps nonpositive; zero stays zero. Verifier is a fixed training signal, not rollout input. Local candidates aren&#x27;t Qwen math rollouts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A positive log ratio on a failure becomes zero, not a sign-flipped extra penalty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24696">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.24696-opdvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0c1bc8524df74367">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-search-plus" data-paper-title="OPDSearch+: Search-Enhanced On-Policy Distillation with Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-opd-search-plus-8653157e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a83045bd25cf420">Should OPDSearch+ students imitate search-result text as their own output?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-search-plus">OPDSearch+: Search-Enhanced On-Policy Distillation with Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Students generate queries, reasoning and answers; search observations condition later actions. Teacher guidance doesn&#x27;t make tool output a student target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use a webpage excerpt to ask the next query rather than role-play the returned page verbatim.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.24310-opd-search-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a83045bd25cf420">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-search-plus" data-paper-title="OPDSearch+: Search-Enhanced On-Policy Distillation with Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-094d17fb80fe1ba6">Why distill from a frozen general teacher before continuing agent RL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-search-plus">OPDSearch+: Search-Enhanced On-Policy Distillation with Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dense guidance on student search traces improves the starting behavior. Verifiable RL then adapts to environmental results rather than remain bound to teacher preferences. No specialized teacher training required; bias and proxy limits remain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn to ask workable queries, then let retrieved evidence and final verification adjust habits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.24310-opd-search-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-094d17fb80fe1ba6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-search-plus" data-paper-title="OPDSearch+: Search-Enhanced On-Policy Distillation with Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a2e884e5827e1ca8">How does on-student search distillation differ from offline teacher demonstrations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-search-plus">OPDSearch+: Search-Enhanced On-Policy Distillation with Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher sees states and prefixes the student actually reached, including mistakes; offline continuations come from teacher states. Different recovery coverage isn&#x27;t a universal performance ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Online scoring sees a wrong first query that a correct teacher demonstration never visits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.24310-opd-search-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a2e884e5827e1ca8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-search-plus" data-paper-title="OPDSearch+: Search-Enhanced On-Policy Distillation with Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bb90580a0607a23c">Does local OPDSearch+ execute real query, reasoning and answer tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-search-plus">OPDSearch+: Search-Enhanced On-Policy Distillation with Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Candidate-level process axes proxy generation/search feedback without real index/model. The real mask covers only generated text, never returned documents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A process score doesn&#x27;t mean a Wikipedia search ran.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.24310-opd-search-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bb90580a0607a23c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:r2-opd" data-paper-title="Beyond Imitation: Filtering On-Policy Distillation by Reasoning Progress" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-r2-opd-a6acbe83" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dfc26c702e1baa99">Why estimate reasoning progress independently in R²-OPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ar2-opd">Beyond Imitation: Filtering On-Policy Distillation by Reasoning Progress</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher preference needn&#x27;t help solve the task. Compare independent progress and mask conflicting supervision rather than equate style with reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A fluent explanation may score high with teacher while moving farther from the solution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.19408-r2-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dfc26c702e1baa99">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:r2-opd" data-paper-title="Beyond Imitation: Filtering On-Policy Distillation by Reasoning Progress" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d2ad241badb27cb1">Why mask conflicting teacher and progress rankings instead of trusting teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ar2-opd">Beyond Imitation: Filtering On-Policy Distillation by Reasoning Progress</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Style can receive teacher approval without useful progress. Independent ordering checks direction. Masking signals uncertainty, not proof a span is wrong, and the progress evaluator still needs validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Don&#x27;t reinforce a polished long explanation if it leaves the key constraint unsolved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.19408-r2-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d2ad241badb27cb1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:r2-opd" data-paper-title="Beyond Imitation: Filtering On-Policy Distillation by Reasoning Progress" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b71496cce2185ce2">How does rank filtering differ from summing rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ar2-opd">Beyond Imitation: Filtering On-Policy Distillation by Reasoning Progress</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Filtering requires agreement to retain teacher signal. Addition lets a large score offset a poor one. Agreement doesn&#x27;t prove either judge correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A huge teacher score cannot buy back a span rejected by progress disagreement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.19408-r2-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b71496cce2185ce2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:r2-opd" data-paper-title="Beyond Imitation: Filtering On-Policy Distillation by Reasoning Progress" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c574e1c32fff2f11">What identities must both R²-OPD rankings share?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ar2-opd">Beyond Imitation: Filtering On-Policy Distillation by Reasoning Progress</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Score the same spans of the same trajectories and align by identity; define ties. Local candidates do not run a real progress judge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Match a span across rankings, not the third list position.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.19408-r2-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c574e1c32fff2f11">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sr-opsd" data-paper-title="SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-sr-opsd-5465332e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4376f7df3fecf6ad">Why keep a reference alongside SR-OPSD self-teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asr-opsd">SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Self-teacher can drift or become overly strong. Reference anchors the geometrically interpolated target and Rényi sensitivity control instead of trusting self-teacher alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retain some prior support when teacher strongly favors a new mode.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09745">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.09745-sr-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4376f7df3fecf6ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sr-opsd" data-paper-title="SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd8058cd01b40f35">Why geometrically mix self-teacher and reference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asr-opsd">SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Log-space combination treats tails and disagreement differently from arithmetic mixtures. Reference anchors, teacher guides and divergence regulates projection sensitivity. Equal endpoints do not make two interpolation methods equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Distributions favoring different tokens can give very different intermediate geometric and arithmetic targets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09745">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.09745-sr-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd8058cd01b40f35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sr-opsd" data-paper-title="SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5fad2e23658437ab">How does geometric interpolation differ from arithmetic averaging?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asr-opsd">SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Combine weighted log probabilities then normalize; arithmetic directly mixes mass. Low support from one side affects them differently, and formulas are not interchangeable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A nearly zero mass on one side can depress a geometric target more than arithmetic average.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09745">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.09745-sr-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5fad2e23658437ab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sr-opsd" data-paper-title="SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-74ebb364ed4fdad0">Why form SR-OPSD targets in log space and normalize explicitly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asr-opsd">SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Power products underflow. Weighted log-space softmax yields a stable distribution on aligned teacher/reference vocabulary. No full model/Rényi experiments locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Raw elementwise product without normalization isn&#x27;t a probability distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09745">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.09745-sr-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-74ebb364ed4fdad0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:u-opsd" data-paper-title="U-OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-u-opsd-4619f519" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-69cb74920e51aa07">Why is U-OPSD privileged view still externally unsupervised?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Au-opsd">U-OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It comes from internal sampling consensus, without external answers/reward or a larger teacher. One view sees an extra internally produced signal, not independently verified truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A short self-selected consensus solution can still be a shared error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.06296-u-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-69cb74920e51aa07">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:u-opsd" data-paper-title="U-OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4ad69881270380a9">How avoid treating shortest consensus as truth without gold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Au-opsd">U-OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Consensus selects a reference and repair targets as pseudo-supervision, not correctness verification. Shared errors may be reinforced. Report internal agreement separately from external holdout and keep gold out of student inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Several responses can use the same wrong formula; the shortest still isn&#x27;t a standard solution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.06296-u-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4ad69881270380a9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:u-opsd" data-paper-title="U-OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2947ac9c36e56042">Why distinguish shortest consensus answer from arbitrary shortest answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Au-opsd">U-OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>First require majority agreement, then minimize length within eligible outputs. The shortest unrestricted may be an empty or outlier answer. Consensus isn&#x27;t gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A short erroneous refusal doesn&#x27;t become privileged guidance because it saves tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.06296-u-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2947ac9c36e56042">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:u-opsd" data-paper-title="U-OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-52f51dfab8f76d12">Can U-OPSD use gold before choosing an internal reference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Au-opsd">U-OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Use predictions only for consensus, thresholds and length. Gold is for independent evaluation. Deterministic mini-suite isn&#x27;t full multi-turn self-distillation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Filtering correctness before voting smuggles answer information into training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.06296-u-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-52f51dfab8f76d12">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rp-opsd" data-paper-title="RP-OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rp-opsd-6ed9619b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-02d09cb456980886">Why distill cross-lingually around reasoning pivots in RP-OPSD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arp-opsd">RP-OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Surface wording differs across languages; state-changing tokens matter more. Compare matched teacher distributions with/without the English reference to locate large information-induced shifts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A connective and a key equation need not receive equal credit based on text differences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06347">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.06347-rp-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-02d09cb456980886">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rp-opsd" data-paper-title="RP-OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e5b5363bc9a06ac0">Why compare matched views with and without English solutions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arp-opsd">RP-OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reference-induced distribution shifts can identify reasoning transitions rather than superficial translation. Concentrate privileged distillation there and keep reference anchoring. Match all other inputs and keep solutions teacher-only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Translated connectives and words determining operation order may shift differently after adding a solution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06347">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.06347-rp-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e5b5363bc9a06ac0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rp-opsd" data-paper-title="RP-OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-60ca89bd820aa23d">How does pivot detection differ from uniformly imitating all English tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arp-opsd">RP-OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Uniform imitation can copy style and translation artifacts. Conditional shifts highlight important positions while retaining reference anchoring. Shifts aren&#x27;t causal truth, so validate teacher quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Different English wording with unchanged mathematical state need not rewrite every student word.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06347">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.06347-rp-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-60ca89bd820aa23d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rp-opsd" data-paper-title="RP-OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f63d2dc1f5e666f">What must the two RP-OPSD teacher views share?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arp-opsd">RP-OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Same model, question and student prefix; remove only reference conditioning. Student rollout cannot see reference answers. Local deterministic proxies aren&#x27;t real multilingual teachers/corpora.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing both model and question prevents attributing probability changes to the English reference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06347">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.06347-rp-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f63d2dc1f5e666f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd2" data-paper-title="On-Policy Delta Distillation for Multilingual Math Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-opd2-d840d7f7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-12b045ccfcff8b40">Why distill the teacher&#x27;s post-training change from base in OPD²?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd2">On-Policy Delta Distillation for Multilingual Math Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NAVER AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher&#x27;s preexisting preferences may not come from target training. The delta emphasizes what changed instead of transferring all language/style bias; matching checkpoints is essential.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unchanged long-sentence preference should not count as newly acquired skill.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05802">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.05802-opd2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-12b045ccfcff8b40">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd2" data-paper-title="On-Policy Delta Distillation for Multilingual Math Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1c97a90289933840">Why copy the delta rather than every teacher preference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd2">On-Policy Delta Distillation for Multilingual Math Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NAVER AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Comparing before/after logp isolates directions associated with post-training instead of inherited language/style/knowledge. It needs comparable checkpoints and isn&#x27;t proven pure capability. Local small distributions don&#x27;t verify language transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If RL improves conclusions but politeness is unchanged, the delta avoids treating the greeting as a new skill.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05802">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.05802-opd2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1c97a90289933840">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd2" data-paper-title="On-Policy Delta Distillation for Multilingual Math Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-942a8457730a05d1">How does delta distillation differ from copying the post-trained distribution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd2">On-Policy Delta Distillation for Multilingual Math Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NAVER AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It subtracts the teacher base; direct matching includes old knowledge and preferences. Subtraction may discard useful information or retain training noise, so not universally better.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learning the update is not copying the whole teacher knowledge base.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05802">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.05802-opd2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-942a8457730a05d1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd2" data-paper-title="On-Policy Delta Distillation for Multilingual Math Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1397d152821b1244">May OPD² use arbitrary teacher families for its two probabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd2">On-Policy Delta Distillation for Multilingual Math Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NAVER AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not silently. Use paired base and post-trained checkpoint on the same prefix with aligned vocabulary/conditioning. Local candidates do not load multilingual math checkpoints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unrelated architecture as base confounds family calibration with the training delta.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05802">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.05802-opd2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1397d152821b1244">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dash" data-paper-title="DASH" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-dash-1d95c042" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2ef1f243013623af">Why propagate later distillation differences to earlier positions in DASH?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adash">DASH</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early choices have multi-step consequences. Local disagreement gates a backward recurrence with adaptive horizon, without extra teacher passes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An early fork causing repeated later errors should see some of their credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.06243-dash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2ef1f243013623af">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dash" data-paper-title="DASH" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-67cd03485d3aa1a0">Why control DASH horizon by local disagreement rather than propagate everything?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adash">DASH</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later teacher feedback may help or become unreliable after divergence. Detached gating varies effective horizon without extra teacher calls. Fixed long or short windows can mix irrelevant signals or miss important outcomes. Gate is not truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Carry future credit across consistent steps but weaken propagation at a severe divergence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.06243-dash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67cd03485d3aa1a0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dash" data-paper-title="DASH" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1844471842da9817">How does DASH&#x27;s continuous gate differ from fixed discount?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adash">DASH</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed discount propagates equally by position; gate uses relative local disagreement to vary horizon. Proxy credit is not always correct and doesn&#x27;t add teacher rollouts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Consequences at equal distance can propagate differently under different local disagreement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.06243-dash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1844471842da9817">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dash" data-paper-title="DASH" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-64ac46dc84be0cdf">How should DASH handle boundaries and gate gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adash">DASH</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recur backward with no next term at sequence end, detach gate and block padding or cross-response propagation. Candidate positions aren&#x27;t long-token traces.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not carry future credit from the next answer into the last token of this one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.06243-dash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-64ac46dc84be0cdf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:causal-opd" data-paper-title="CausalOPD: First-Wrong-Step Supervision for Distilling Causal Chain Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-causal-opd-da48af2a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6817fdf23c677be4">Why prioritize the first error in CausalOPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acausal-opd">CausalOPD: First-Wrong-Step Supervision for Distilling Causal Chain Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later errors can follow from an early break. Short repair at its source avoids redundant punishment, then a curriculum moves evidence→mechanism→conclusion. Teacher localization must be reliable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An incorrect premise can make later coherent derivation wrong.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03673">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.03673-causal-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6817fdf23c677be4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:causal-opd" data-paper-title="CausalOPD: First-Wrong-Step Supervision for Distilling Causal Chain Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f522c88f42ea42cb">Why locate the earliest wrong step and use short-horizon repair?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acausal-opd">CausalOPD: First-Wrong-Step Supervision for Distilling Causal Chain Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later mistakes can inherit an earlier false premise. Correct the turning point rather than imitate final conclusions, then organize evidence/mechanism/conclusion. The teacher can misidentify it; proxy diagnostics aren&#x27;t causal reasoning capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repair the first confusion of correlation with causation, not just the last sentence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03673">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.03673-causal-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f522c88f42ea42cb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:causal-opd" data-paper-title="CausalOPD: First-Wrong-Step Supervision for Distilling Causal Chain Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d075ec8aeb8c068">What tradeoff separates short first-error repairs and whole-trajectory imitation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acausal-opd">CausalOPD: First-Wrong-Step Supervision for Distilling Causal Chain Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Short windows focus local breaks and reduce irrelevant supervision; full imitation covers more but may diverge from student behavior. Incorrect localization can miss the real error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fixing one mechanism link doesn&#x27;t guarantee every conclusion is correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03673">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.03673-causal-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d075ec8aeb8c068">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:causal-opd" data-paper-title="CausalOPD: First-Wrong-Step Supervision for Distilling Causal Chain Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7620ef1fddd551e7">May first-error search default to index zero if nothing is found?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acausal-opd">CausalOPD: First-Wrong-Step Supervision for Distilling Causal Chain Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Explicitly represent no error or unreliable judgment. Align step indices and keep privileged diagnosis out of inference. Local candidates don&#x27;t implement the full causal teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An empty list must not invent a first-step error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03673">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.03673-causal-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7620ef1fddd551e7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pcsd" data-paper-title="PCSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-pcsd-bac5e7a6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a3012558b9e6ffd8">Why use persistent signals rather than one token gap in PCSD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apcsd">PCSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local gaps are noisy; one whole-response weight is coarse. Accumulate support in adaptive windows, decay declining trends and continuously gate supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One high teacher score should differ from several supported consecutive steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01837">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.01837-pcsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a3012558b9e6ffd8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pcsd" data-paper-title="PCSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-285b4151125240b5">Why accumulate sustained teacher-favoring evidence rather than switch on single gaps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apcsd">PCSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Single differences are noisy while whole-response weights hide position. Windowed exponential accumulation and decline decay combine smooth OPSD/GRPO gates. Persistence stabilizes signals without proving teacher correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An isolated overestimated word need not receive the same supervision as a consistently supported passage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01837">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.01837-pcsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-285b4151125240b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pcsd" data-paper-title="PCSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9458370561212e7b">How does PCSD continuous gating differ from a hard threshold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apcsd">PCSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sigmoid varies strength smoothly; accumulated trends allow the same present gap to receive different weights. It still relies on teacher quality, not a new verifier.</p>
