<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal current gaps can differ if one has risen consistently and the other fallen.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01837">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.01837-pcsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9458370561212e7b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pcsd" data-paper-title="PCSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f566044b5882cab1">May PCSD accumulation continue across independent responses?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apcsd">PCSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Reset per response and apply valid masks. Teacher/gate statistics are fixed supervision; deterministic checks aren&#x27;t long-reasoning training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Previous problem&#x27;s ending support cannot become the next one&#x27;s prior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01837">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.01837-pcsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f566044b5882cab1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:flux-opd" data-paper-title="Flux-OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-flux-opd-da1bf9b3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-51ae4d316a0e75fb">Why keep a context-free anchor in Flux-OPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aflux-opd">Flux-OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Students can absorb fixed context, but replacing it can abruptly change targets. The anchor stays fixed and accepts relative corrections from evolving contexts rather than wholesale replacement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new retrieval background can change one judgment without moving all language targets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28022">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.28022-flux-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-51ae4d316a0e75fb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:flux-opd" data-paper-title="Flux-OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1307998183aef378">Why use a fixed anchor and conflict-weighted context corrections?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aflux-opd">Flux-OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Replacing context can make targets jump. Relative corrections preserve the context-free base; geometric overlap weakens disagreement. Its normalization constant isn&#x27;t arbitrary pairwise opinion distance. Local axes do not perform real extraction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For opposing suggested reasoning paths, retain the shared anchor and attenuate corrections rather than follow every new prompt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28022">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.28022-flux-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1307998183aef378">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:flux-opd" data-paper-title="Flux-OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f7862bd835149bd">Why weaken Flux-OPD corrections when geometric teacher views conflict?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aflux-opd">Flux-OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Geometric normalization reflects overlap. Large conflict reduces effective correction instead of averaging incompatible suggestions forcefully. Agreement also doesn&#x27;t prove correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two confident opposing answers should not receive twice the trust.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28022">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.28022-flux-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f7862bd835149bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:flux-opd" data-paper-title="Flux-OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f82a9f25cb450f9a">Do local Flux reward axes reproduce real evolving-context extraction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aflux-opd">Flux-OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. They proxy teacher changes without video, medical or language context models. Build log-space targets relative to one anchor; don&#x27;t mix differences from unrelated baselines.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two hand-built logit tensors don&#x27;t implement document extraction and updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28022">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.28022-flux-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f82a9f25cb450f9a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:beta-opsd" data-paper-title="β-OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-beta-opsd-d0fa334d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-977ed9994d46ab37">Why view β-OPSD as a case of regularized policy optimization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Abeta-opsd">β-OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reference and privileged teacher define a geometric target; token-logit distillation replaces expensive policy optimization. β has the derivation&#x27;s specific role, not arbitrary mixture weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Same guidance with different regularization yields different effective targets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28582">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.28582-beta-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-977ed9994d46ab37">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:beta-opsd" data-paper-title="β-OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f8dd46538565b98">Why combine geometric teacher/reference interpolation with return-to-go?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Abeta-opsd">β-OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Interpolation controls target direction/strength; return-to-go controls temporal credit. Vanilla is a specific setting, not proof arbitrary logit averages solve the same objective. Local positions aren&#x27;t long sequences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>How much to trust teacher and how far later errors influence early choices are separate decisions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28582">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.28582-beta-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f8dd46538565b98">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:beta-opsd" data-paper-title="β-OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e7ca26ca125c53d6">How does return-to-go differ from a current-token log gap?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Abeta-opsd">β-OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It accumulates discounted future gaps, assigning later consequences to current decisions. Longer horizons can add variance and depend on termination; not automatically more accurate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A single early error can cause several later deviations invisible to immediate gap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28582">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.28582-beta-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e7ca26ca125c53d6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:beta-opsd" data-paper-title="β-OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b67e3d6fcf8f3b01">Does local β-OPSD execute long CoT with its linear-position proxy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Abeta-opsd">β-OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Candidate actions and linear returns replace tokens/trajectory positions. Freeze teacher/reference and preserve ordering; proxy results aren&#x27;t Qwen LoRA evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Suffix sums over a few numbers don&#x27;t demonstrate equivalent credit in real generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28582">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.28582-beta-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b67e3d6fcf8f3b01">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:relay-opd" data-paper-title="Relay-OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-relay-opd-4c82d340" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4c5c0714ca895fa4">Why let Relay-OPD teacher briefly take over then return control?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arelay-opd">Relay-OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An invalid prefix can trap future learning. Short, budgeted intervention returns to a learnable region while student still acts after handoff.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher repairs a few critical steps, then student finishes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26057">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.26057-relay-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4c5c0714ca895fa4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:relay-opd" data-paper-title="Relay-OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4000dc4715f9afd">Why not count a relayed trace as purely student on-policy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arelay-opd">Relay-OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher generates intervened actions and changes later student conditioning. It is a mixture. Budget keeps help local and provenance tracks writers. Include teacher cost and don&#x27;t claim independent success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A student finishing after two teacher steps need not succeed unaided.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26057">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.26057-relay-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4000dc4715f9afd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:relay-opd" data-paper-title="Relay-OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a402188342475001">How do relayed traces differ from native student rollouts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arelay-opd">Relay-OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher intervention changes action sources and states; log takeover interval and budget. Teacher-assisted success is not autonomous student success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher bypassing a hard step requires separate no-teacher evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26057">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.26057-relay-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a402188342475001">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:relay-opd" data-paper-title="Relay-OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6efb3d89fabed8cc">How does the Relay state machine prevent budget overrun?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arelay-opd">Relay-OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Track cumulative handoff lengths, enforce total and record takeover/return/termination. Local teacher is cached candidate distribution, not real Qwen or eight-GPU training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Once budget is spent, do not start a second handoff.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26057">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.26057-relay-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6efb3d89fabed8cc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-lm" data-paper-title="OPDLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-opd-lm-752e6c98" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bcaf27448b12ef0f">Why distill an AR teacher on a diffusion student&#x27;s own decoding path in OPDLM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-lm">OPDLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Texas A&amp;M University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Moving to bidirectional denoising can forget learned behavior. Random masks can miss confidence-decoding states. Actual student rollouts reduce mismatch with inference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train on the reveal order actually visited, not only random masking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06712">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.06712-opd-lm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bcaf27448b12ef0f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-lm" data-paper-title="OPDLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e0f2193c9ec3461">Why distill along actual bidirectional decoding rather than random masks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-lm">OPDLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Texas A&amp;M University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Confidence decoding visits different contexts and attention conversion can cause forgetting. Score student-visited states with frozen AR targets while retaining its causal condition. Different visible evidence cannot be equated positionwise arbitrarily.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A confidence-first reveal produces contexts random-mask training might never encounter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06712">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.06712-opd-lm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e0f2193c9ec3461">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-lm" data-paper-title="OPDLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-027b88cbb7da4e67">Do AR teacher and bidirectional student see the same information at a position?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-lm">OPDLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Texas A&amp;M University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. AR teacher scores causal history, student denoises visible unmasked tokens. Align positions and state what each sees instead of treating conditioning differences as quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Student may see a revealed token to the right while teacher sees only left context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06712">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.06712-opd-lm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-027b88cbb7da4e67">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-lm" data-paper-title="OPDLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6310389653a271ec">Where should OPDLM compute loss and does teacher update?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-lm">OPDLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Texas A&amp;M University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use specified masked/supervised positions, freeze AR teacher and align logits to student trajectories. Mini-suite does not fully convert/train a real bidirectional LM.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Including already determined tokens changes denoising supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06712">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.06712-opd-lm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6310389653a271ec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gkd" data-paper-title="GKD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-gkd-c556ce32" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4c524a8349360e89">Why does GKD ask a teacher to score student-generated prefixes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agkd">GKD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher paths can be idealized and miss visited errors. Sample student trajectories and ask for full teacher distributions at those prefixes, teaching recovery without only copying demonstrations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher can guide next actions after the student&#x27;s second step goes wrong.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.13649">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4c524a8349360e89">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gkd" data-paper-title="GKD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8925a124ecc2e55c">Why does same-prefix teacher scoring reach student mistakes better than complete teacher answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agkd">GKD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed teacher trajectories avoid many student errors. Teacher distributions on sampled student prefixes reach those states; data fraction controls fixed/on-policy mixture. Coverage doesn&#x27;t guarantee teacher recovery or determine divergence choice.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A correct demonstration never visits the student&#x27;s wrong step, while prefix scoring can help from that actual state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.13649">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8925a124ecc2e55c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gkd" data-paper-title="GKD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-703130a0c5c1bd0e">Is GKD student data fraction the same as IPD token mixing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agkd">GKD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. GKD controls training-source mix of fixed and student traces. IPD mixes policies at each state. Dataset mixtures and one-step mixtures generally visit different trajectories.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Half the batch from fixed answers is not choosing teacher with 50% probability at every token.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.13649">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-703130a0c5c1bd0e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gkd" data-paper-title="GKD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0678c0b8f189aef5">Why specify which distribution comes first in GKD KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agkd">GKD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Forward/reverse KL and generalized JSD differ in coverage and concentration. Freeze teacher on identical student prefixes. Candidate teacher distributions aren&#x27;t real T5 translation/summarization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>KL(T||S) and KL(S||T) yield different gradients despite both being KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.13649">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0678c0b8f189aef5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:minillm" data-paper-title="MiniLLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-minillm-8f5f3ddd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d5b1df040633afb">Why favor reverse KL in MiniLLM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aminillm">MiniLLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Small students may not cover all teacher modes. Reverse KL concentrates on student-supported reliable teacher regions, possibly missing modes. Sharpness isn&#x27;t always desirable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn several reliable phrasings rather than spread over all teacher continuations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.08543">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2306.08543-minillm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d5b1df040633afb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:minillm" data-paper-title="MiniLLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-446e1e3109c8e57a">How does reverse KL affect small students&#x27; treatment of teacher tails?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aminillm">MiniLLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Student expectation focuses capacity on visited teacher-supported modes; forward KL covers teacher mass. Direction changes gradients and expectation. Preserve teacher-mixed stabilization; candidate checks aren&#x27;t long-text distillation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A limited student may concentrate on a few reliable phrasings rather than cover every rare teacher expression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.08543">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2306.08543-minillm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-446e1e3109c8e57a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:minillm" data-paper-title="MiniLLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-668adaf234eb9d00">What coverage tradeoff separates MiniLLM from forward KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aminillm">MiniLLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Forward emphasizes teacher-mass coverage; reverse follows student-sampled modes. Teacher-mixed sampling and variance reduction also matter; direction alone isn&#x27;t the full method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Few reliable modes versus many weak modes requires task evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.08543">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2306.08543-minillm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-668adaf234eb9d00">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:minillm" data-paper-title="MiniLLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d3b8dc61e2654a7c">Whose distribution defines MiniLLM reverse-KL expectation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aminillm">MiniLLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Student, with explicit teacher-mixed sampling and corrections in practice. Arbitrary fixed teacher text is not a substitute. Local candidates lack real tokenizer, long generation and GPT judging.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scoring teacher solutions with a KL-looking formula doesn&#x27;t provide student on-policy coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.08543">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2306.08543-minillm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d3b8dc61e2654a7c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mpopd" data-paper-title="Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-mpopd-f637bd45" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea8497388e70559c">How does MPOPD mixing a rollout policy differ from mixing a student target?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ampopd">Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A learned proposal changes which prefixes are visited. The student still minimizes reverse KL to the teacher and corrects the old proposal/student gap. Training against a mixed target changes the loss without necessarily visiting teacher-supported paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reweighting observed bad paths cannot generate a rare good path that was never collected. A changed proposal may sample it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36477v2">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.36477-mpopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea8497388e70559c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mpopd" data-paper-title="Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-73cdf4d1f29b5fcc">Which importance weight multiplies the student&#x27;s KL at position j?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ampopd">Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Eq. 7 uses the one-step ratio w[j−1], with weight 1 at the first prefix. Use frozen old student and proposal probabilities of the sampled token and clip. Neither current-token ratio nor cumulative product is correct; no recomputation by the updating student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Ratios 4, 0.25, 4 yield KL weights [1,4,0.25], not [4,0.25,4] or [1,4,1].</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地结果与负控. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36477v2">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.36477-mpopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-73cdf4d1f29b5fcc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mpopd" data-paper-title="Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-adae83b8adbaabec">Does fixed-eta geometric mixing equal a probability average or a fixed KL radius?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ampopd">Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Neither. It adds weighted log probabilities before normalization, not probabilities. Distributions vary by prefix, so the same eta produces different KL movement. A fixed local radius can imply prefix-specific eta; the global setting is a computational compromise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Eta 0.4 barely moves a prefix where teacher and student agree but moves more mass when they conflict.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36477v2">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.36477-mpopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-adae83b8adbaabec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mpopd" data-paper-title="Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-54bb7083c4215957">Why don&#x27;t real gradients establish full MPOPD integration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ampopd">Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The tensor kernel has no sampler, LM copy or teacher call. Each round must reset proposal from the updated student and optimize it toward the new geometric target. Student KL and target are renormalized on the same teacher top-k support. Numeric checks do not verify trajectory origins, resets or extended training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Cached old prefixes backpropagate but aren&#x27;t current proposal rollouts. A small CUDA tensor check is not accuracy on 16 reasoning benchmarks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 数据协议与实现边界, 代码映射, 高成本完整实验. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36477v2">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.36477-mpopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-54bb7083c4215957">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

If a student generates from its own mistaken prefixes at inference, why might imitating complete teacher answers miss those states?

## Takeaway

Autoregressive students visit their own prefixes at inference. GKD generates with the student and asks the teacher to supervise distributions on those states, reducing train–test state mismatch. MiniLLM shows that divergence direction changes which teacher probability mass a student covers. Track where trajectories come from, which prefix both models see, and how discrepancies become updates. MPOPD learns a separate proposal that samples near the geometric mixture of teacher and student. Student loss, proposal loss, and frozen one-step ratios have different roles, so trajectory distillation need not sample directly from the current student.

## Example

The teacher first computes area then a ratio; the student writes the wrong formula. SFT on teacher prefixes may never teach recovery. OPD can query teacher probabilities on the student's prefix, but the teacher might also follow the mistake. Better coverage does not guarantee correct supervision; check teacher quality, divergence, and validation.

## Common pitfall

Scoring student trajectories is not generating a new teacher answer or transferring all teacher capabilities. KL values, finite gradients, and candidate diagnostics support local mechanisms. Lightweight GKD and MiniLLM do not reproduce full checkpoint training. Multiple numerical seeds are not a capability comparison.

## Reading order

Read GKD to separate sampling from teacher scoring, MiniLLM for divergence direction and sampling stabilization, and Learning Signals to distinguish high loss from a useful learning direction.

1. [GKD](../../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.13649)
2. [MiniLLM](../../../../post-training/2306.08543-minillm/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.08543)
3. [Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals](../../../../post-training/2610.11247-opd-learning-signals/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11247)

## Check your understanding

Does training ten times on cached teacher answers make the data student-on-policy?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    No. The trajectories remain fixed teacher samples. Check which student policy sampled, and whether the teacher supervised on student prefixes. Offline student replay still needs a distribution-shift and update contract; the label “student” does not make it current on-policy data.

</details>
